capability: Bounded, observed terminal phase for external tool processes (F03/F06, ADR 0081): the cancellation callback only signals, one runner-owned termination work item and one total 5-second host deadline bound every wait after the terminal signal, detached still-running work keeps handle custody until it settles and is finished exception-safely, a process-wide hard capacity (owner decision 92) atomically reserves a slot before starting so invocations that are running or still cleaning up never exceed the limit and a new run is refused with a typed error carrying restart guidance beyond it, and a typed cleanup observation on which the staged processors and the trust probe fail closed
searchEvidence: rg -n 'SystemExternalProcessRunner|IExternalProcessRunner|BoundedProcessOutputReader|ExternalProcessResult' src tests: one production runner (SystemExternalProcessRunner) and one drain helper (BoundedProcessOutputReader); production consumers are ExternalCombinerProcessor, LegacyCombinerPostbuildProcessor and RuntimeTrustProbeProcess; every other implementation is a test fake that constructs ExternalProcessResult positionally, so the new Cleanup init property defaults to Complete for them.

SPEC.md item 27, docs/adr/0006-external-combiner-tool-runner.md (common host owns timeout/cancellation and process-tree cleanup; any timeout or crash fails closed) and docs/architecture/external-combiner-tool-runner.md name the Infrastructure execution host as the owner; AUD-02 (docs/architecture/post-v1.1.8-audit-handoff.md) names SystemExternalProcessRunner / BoundedProcessOutputReader and asks one owner to bound termination confirmation and pipe drain. ADR 0006 does not define the observation scope, deadline or fault/cancellation priority; new ADR 0081 (number allocated by the commander) records them and amends ADR 0006.

rg -n '\.Kill\(|WaitForExitAsync|WaitForExit\(|JobObject' src: the other termination owners are VersionManagement-only (ManagedProcessTermination: synchronous kill, 5 s wait, uncertainty = AggregateException/InvalidOperationException/Win32Exception; StableLauncherHandoff TerminationUnconfirmed observation budget; ManagedProcessLifetimeLease job object; WindowsContainedProcessStarter 5 s confirmation for a failed suspended start). None drains redirected streams, and ProjectDependencyTests forbid NvtFwCombiner.Infrastructure from referencing VersionManagement.Infrastructure. The runner is extended with the same uncertainty classification plus NotSupportedException; no second external-tool execution path is added and none of those owners changes.

rg -n 'external-tool\.process\.' src tests docs: issue codes are produced only by the two staged processors; no schema or localization table enumerates them. One new code (external-tool.process.cleanup-incomplete) is used only for a zero exit with incomplete cleanup; timeout and non-zero exit keep their codes and append the cleanup sentence.

Reproduced at 557a9ee6a with a harness over the public runner API: a descendant that denies PROCESS_TERMINATE makes CancellationTokenSource.Cancel() throw AggregateException(Win32Exception 5) and RunAsync fault with it on cancellation and on timeout; a background grandchild holding stdout extends a 2 s timeout run to 10.4 s after a natural exit and to 10.2 s when orphaned outside the tree walk; cancellation during that drain returns exit 0. An unbounded wait after a kill that produces no exit has no real OS reproduction yet and is covered by a seam.

F19 ownership is preserved: ProcessLaunchGate.Start and ExternalStagingDirectory.TryAcquire/Dispose are not changed; a surviving descendant can keep the staging directory as its current directory, and the existing Dispose already tolerates that IOException.

Owner decision 92 (wave2 head 5ed61fded) bounds detached unsettled cleanup. The runner adds a process-wide DetachedCleanupBudget shared by all instances via the static Production seam, so ExternalCombinerProcessor, LegacyCombinerPostbuildProcessor and RuntimeTrustProbeProcess.CreateDefault share one count. It is a hard cap, not a pre-check: TryReserve is a compare-and-set that only takes a slot below the limit, so reserved-plus-detached never exceeds the limit under concurrent starts; the reservation is returned exactly once. Limit 8: external-tool runs are effectively serial per workflow (one UI run or CLI invocation at a time; ADR 0075 preload workers are not external tools), so more than a handful of simultaneously held or stuck cleanups is a host fault, and 8 leaves headroom for rare transient slow terminations while bounding resources to a small constant. Refusal is a typed ExternalProcessCleanupCapacityException thrown before ProcessLaunchGate.Start, mapped to a new external-tool.process.cleanup-capacity issue (no schema or localization table enumerates external-tool.* codes, confirmed by rg).

F-11 (third review): RuntimeTrustProbeProcess.VerifyAsync returns a RuntimeTrustProbeVerdict (issue code plus optional user message) instead of a bare code, so a capacity refusal keeps runtime.trust.probe-failed while carrying the restart message; ToolchainRuntimeCandidateInspector surfaces that message in the inspection result instead of the generic 'Windows could not verify' text. This adds ToolchainRuntimeCandidateInspector.cs to the mutable paths (an existing R2 Infrastructure file, unchanged owner).

Fourth review (codex/gpt-6-astra, patch 15f5455e...): F-12 the concurrency test called RunAsync in sequence, so reservations did not truly race; now dedicated threads are released together by one Barrier and a separate test hammers TryReserve from 32 barrier-released threads for 200 rounds. F-13 Finish() could skip later disposals, the slot return and the signal when a disposal threw; now each disposal is independent, faults are observed, the slot is always returned in a finally, a distinct ResourcesReleaseFailed signal replaces the success signal, and the detached continuation is observed (fault-injection tests on the inline and detached paths). F-14 the refusal wording and the public InUseInvocations field (renamed from DetachedInvocations) now describe running-or-cleaning-up capacity and use the value observed by the compare-and-set; internal names follow (ExternalProcessCapacity, Capacity seam). F-15 design-document lifecycle corrected.

Fifth review (codex/gpt-6-astra, patch 6faea65a...): F-16 the concurrency test exit seam turned an opened gate into a successful exit, so the runner could read ExitCode before the process had exited; the seam now waits for the gate and then for the real process.WaitForExitAsync(observationToken), a cancelled observation surfaces as cancellation, and each admitted run is asserted to return exit code 0 with complete cleanup. The blocking termination seam had the same pattern and now performs the real tree kill after its gate. F-17 ADR item 10 restored to its own line; ADR wording now says the atomic reservation (not necessarily a compare-and-set) observed the refusal count and scopes ResourcesReleaseFailed to an internal test-observer phase. The environment-dependent real-OS refused-termination fixture removed in revision 5 stays removed; the reviewer accepted relying on the refusal seams, and no text claims that a real-OS refused-termination scenario was re-run.
semanticOwner: Infrastructure.ExternalTools.SystemExternalProcessRunner remains the only owner of an external tool invocation's terminal phase: the terminal signal, the single termination work item, exit confirmation, redirected-stream drain and reader stop under one host deadline, custody of detached work, and the cleanup observation. BoundedProcessOutputReader remains its bounded drain helper. ExternalCombinerProcessor and LegacyCombinerPostbuildProcessor keep the mapping from the typed runner result to fail-closed CompositionIssue codes; RuntimeTrustProbeProcess keeps its runtime.trust.* mapping. Application, Presentation and CLI code and their classification channels are unchanged.
terminalContract: Per ADR 0081. RunAsync starts through ProcessLaunchGate unchanged, after a detached-cleanup budget check (below). The caller's cancellation callback only completes a signal, so Cancel() returns without process work. The terminal signal is the first of natural exit, manifest timeout, caller cancellation or a failed exit observation; a cancellation already requested wins. At most one tree termination runs per invocation, on a background task: at once after timeout, cancellation or failed exit observation, and after a natural exit only when a stream stays open past the 2 s held-output grace. Every host wait after the signal shares one total 5 s deadline (owner decision 86), computed by one Schedule(signaledAt) that places the reader-stop point at deadline minus reserve (inside the deadline, not added after it) and the deadline at signaledAt plus 5 s; the deadline is a host constant, not a manifest or profile timeout. The run returns within the deadline; work still running is detached, keeps custody (process handle, stream readers and cancellation sources are disposed only after every background task settles, late faults observed then), and the finally path always releases and requests termination if the exit was never observed. It does not claim no handle survives 5 s. Termination exceptions (AggregateException, Win32Exception, InvalidOperationException, NotSupportedException, or any other fault of the termination task), exit-observation faults and reader faults are classified, never thrown. Caller cancellation requested before the decision point ends as OperationCanceledException bound to the caller token, its message naming the observed cleanup; later cancellation does not change the result. Otherwise the result is ExternalProcessResult(exit code on natural exit else -1, TimedOut on timeout, bounded stdout, bounded stderr) with Cleanup = Complete, TerminationUnconfirmed, OutputStreamHeldOpen or OutputReadFailed, in that priority from TerminationUnconfirmed down. Each cleanup value's diagnostic text states only the observation and never names a holder the runner cannot identify. Complete is an observation of the direct child and its two streams, not a proof that every descendant stopped; a descendant holding no stream is invisible (owner decision 85). Invocation capacity (owner decision 92): a process-wide hard cap, fixed limit 8, counting invocations that are running or still cleaning up. RunAsync atomically reserves one slot (compare-and-set below the limit) before ProcessLaunchGate.Start, so the in-use count never exceeds the limit under concurrency; a detached invocation keeps its original slot, and the slot is returned exactly once, on start failure, completion, or when detached work settles (including after a disposal failure). At the cap RunAsync throws ExternalProcessCleanupCapacityException before starting any process; its InUseInvocations is the count the atomic reservation observed at the refusal (from the initial read when the capacity was already full, or from a failed compare-and-set), and the user message states only that runs still running or still cleaning up filled the capacity, with restart guidance and no count. The final step disposes each handle independently, observes every disposal fault, always returns the slot, and then publishes exactly one signal: ResourcesReleased when every disposal succeeded, otherwise ResourcesReleaseFailed; the detached continuation is observed. Both signals are internal phases published only to the test observer seam; production has no observer, log or user notification for them, so they are not a public notification contract. Because running invocations count, normal runs behave as before only while fewer than the limit are in use at once. Consumers: a consumer may use captured output as a successful result or protocol input only when Cleanup is Complete, though the captured text may still be quoted as error diagnostics for a timeout or non-zero exit. Timeout keeps external-tool.process.timeout and non-zero exit keeps external-tool.process.failed, both appending the cleanup sentence; a zero exit with Cleanup != Complete fails closed as external-tool.process.cleanup-incomplete before any staged file or output is read as a result, and a postbuild command sequence stops before its next command; the capacity refusal maps to external-tool.process.cleanup-capacity (staged processors) or runtime.trust.probe-failed (trust probe), and the trust probe carries the capacity reason and a restart message to the inspection result so ToolchainRuntimeCandidateInspector shows recovery guidance instead of the generic verification failure. RuntimeTrustProbeProcess keeps timeout priority: a timed-out probe is runtime.trust.timeout, and only a non-timed-out incomplete cleanup is runtime.trust.probe-failed. Output bytes, ranges, order, CRC/Header, naming, manifests and profiles are unchanged; a run whose tool exits cleanly with both streams ended behaves exactly as before.
